data.hypothesis: For each 128-thread CTA, replacing the modulo-based tree and its repeated CTA barriers with four warp reductions, one CTA barrier, and a warp-0 combine should reduce local synchronization and conditional work. The input loading, launch geometry, multi-stage scratch schedule, and final copy remain unchanged, so the overall timing may still be dominated by traffic or launch overhead.
data.notes: The proposal preserves one input per lane and zero-fills tail lanes; all reductions remain integer additions. No candidate checks or timings were run here. Compare controller correctness results and complete-run timings against baseline-e1 before deciding whether the local change helps.
transformations: Replace reduce0's modulo-based shared-memory tree with a warp shuffle reduction for each warp.
Store one partial per warp, synchronize once per CTA, then combine the four partials in warp zero.
Zero-fill out-of-range lane values and keep the existing 128-thread launch, stage schedule, scratch selection, and final copy unchanged.
